why: With exactly one '*', a pattern splits into a prefix and a suffix; the text matches iff it starts with the prefix, ends with the suffix, and is long enough that the two do not overlap. That is a comparison from both ends inward, the two-pointer idea, with no regex or DP needed.
hints: There is exactly one star. What must the text look like before it and after it?
Split pat at '*' into pre and suf. The text matches when it starts with pre, ends with suf, and len(pre) + len(suf) <= len(text), so the star covers a non-negative middle.
For each pair, compare pre against the front and suf against the back (pointers from both ends). O(|text| + |pat|) per query.
pitfalls: Overlap: text "ab" with pattern "ab*b" has prefix and suffix both present but overlapping; it must be NO. Check the length condition.
An empty prefix or empty suffix ("*abc", "abc*") must still work; text[-0:] in Python is the whole string, so guard empty suffix.
No built-in regex is allowed by the source.
